content: Leucine-rich alpha-2-glycoprotein 1 (LRG1) is a protein in humans that is encoded by the LRG1 gene. The leucine-rich repeat (LRR) family of proteins, which includes LRG1, is known to play roles in protein-protein interactions, signal transduction, cell adhesion, and cellular development. LRG1 is specifically expressed during the differentiation of granulocytes. LRG1 has been demonstrated to promote neovascularization, which refers to the formation of new blood vessels. It achieves this by altering the signaling of transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-beta) in endothelial cells. LRG1 binds to the accessory receptor endoglin and facilitates signaling through the ALK1-Smad1/5/8 pathway. Elevated levels of the LRG protein have been observed in cases of acute appendicitis, suggesting its potential use as a diagnostic biomarker for this condition. Additionally, LRG1 may serve as a therapeutic target for diseases characterized by abnormal neovascularization.
